title: AI data centre's biggest infrastructure challenge? JP Morgan CEO Jamie Dimon says it’s electricity
source_used: The Times of India (Bloomberg TV interview)
key_facts: JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon spoke in an interview with Bloomberg TV, reported by The Times of India on 8 Oct 2026.
He said data centre developers should prioritise places where communities support such projects: 'There are a lot of states that would take it that have access to power'.
The Times of India links this to debates over electricity use, land and local strain from data centres.
In the same interview Dimon said AI risks 'went up 10-fold after Mythos', Anthropic's model.
He said he would not 'get hysterical' about whether AI is existential, and that his firm is working to fix problems.
quote_evidence: “There are a lot of states that would take it that have access to power,” Dimon said, highlighting the growing challenge of finding suitable sites for the massive facilities needed to support AI workloads.
According to Dimon, risks from AI “went up 10-fold after Mythos.”
“I’m not going to get hysterical over, ‘Is it existential or not?’ What we’re doing is rolling up our sleeves and going to work to fix it.”
why_it_matters_hint: The head of the largest US bank links where AI data centres can be built to access to electricity and local support.
event_date: Interview date not stated; Times of India report 8 Oct 2026 (IST)
notes: Firstpost original blocked (403). The Times of India report covers a Bloomberg TV interview with the same speaker and topic; assumed to be the same interview as Firstpost's, but Firstpost's headline claim that electricity is the 'biggest' challenge is not worded that way in the Times of India text.
